title: The per-row failure marker reads the same judgement as the indicator
outcome: `hasFailedWrite` marks an Entry List row only when its write can never succeed, matching the standard the indicator's 送不出去 condition already uses. A row whose write has merely exhausted its backoff heals itself and is no longer marked as failed.
acceptanceCriteria: This narrows the criterion S08 of `retryable-entry-writes` established ('exhausted its attempts') to 'the last error is not retryable' -- the two used to coincide because a spent backoff and a hopeless error both set `nextAttemptAt: null`, and S01 of `retryable-queue-persistence` already separated them for the queue-level status; this slice brings the per-row marker in line with the same distinction.

The reason for narrowing: an entry that only ran out of backoff heals itself on the next flush or `online` event, so marking its row with a destructive ring the whole time it waits is the per-row version of the over-warning this Change removes at the indicator level.
A row whose entry has `attempts >= 2` but a retryable (or absent) `lastError` shows no failure marker, matching the indicator's 待送 (not 送不出去) treatment of the same entry.
A row whose entry's `lastError` is not retryable still shows the marker and its retry control, unchanged from S08's behaviour.
